HeartbeatRequest.description: Every player a proxy still holds, in one call. Batched because a proxy with a thousand players would otherwise send a thousand requests per interval.

playerIds.description: Player UUIDs. One malformed id rejects the whole batch.

missing.description: Ids with no session. Not an error: the player logged out between the proxy building this batch and the write landing.

LoginRequest.description: A proxy claiming the network-wide session for a player.

playerName.description: The name the player logged in with. Optional, but a session created without one cannot be found by name until the player reconnects.

proxyId.description: The proxy the player connected to. Optional, and worth sending: a login that names its proxy can take a session over from a different one, which is what a proxy-to-proxy transfer looks like from here. A login without it can only wait out the session TTL.

region.description: Where that proxy is. Absent is a legitimate answer, not an error.

NameLookupResponse.description: Player id to name, for players who need not be online.

names.description: Ids this service has never seen are absent rather than mapped to a placeholder every caller would have to recognise.

locale.description: BCP-47 language tag. Null when the player has never chosen one — the caller falls back to the locale the client announces.

PlayerSession.description: A player's live session: who they are and where.

playerName.description: Absent for a session created by a proxy that sent no name.

proxyId.description: The proxy holding the player. Absent for sessions created before proxies declared one.

serverName.description: The backend server the player is on. Absent while they are still on the proxy.

region.description: Where the proxy is. Absent means unknown, which is normal — sessions outlive a rollout.

Problem.description: A failed request, in RFC 9457 problem-details form.

status.description: HTTP status, repeated in the body.

detail.description: What went wrong with this specific request.
examples: The player already holds a session on another proxy.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, not on the prose.

ProxyCounts.description: Players per proxy and region, network-wide.

proxies.description: One entry per proxy holding at least one player.

total.description: Everyone online network-wide, which equals the sum of `proxies` — every session belongs to exactly one proxy, unlike backend servers where a player may be on none.

ProxyPlayerCount.description: One proxy's share of the network.

region.description: Absent when the session predates the proxy declaring a region.

servers.description: One entry per server holding at least one player. A server nobody is on is absent rather than zero — the caller knows its own server list and can render the rest as empty.

total.description: Everyone online network-wide. Counts players who have not reached a backend server yet, so it can exceed the sum of `servers`.

ServerPlayerCount.description: One backend server's share of the network.

SetLocaleRequest.description: Store or clear a language preference.

locale.description: The tag to store; null or blank clears the preference. Stored verbatim — the caller validates it against the languages it actually ships.

UpdateServerRequest.description: The backend server a player has moved to.

bearerAuth.description: The projected ServiceAccount token from /var/run/secrets/grounds/token, with the grounds-services audience.

info.description:
Network-wide player presence: who is online, on which proxy and backend server, under what name, and in which language they want to be spoken to.

A proxy only knows the players connected to itself, so anything that spans proxies — a private message, a party invite, an accurate player count — has to ask here. The session table is the network's single answer to "is this player online"; a login is a claim on it, and a second one is refused.

Sessions are presence and are deleted on logout. Names outlive them: a separate, never-deleted index is written at every login, which is what lets a leaderboard or a match history show a name rather than a raw UUID.

get.description: How the network is spread across proxies and where those proxies are — what `/online` asks. A separate call from the server counts rather than another field on their response: the two group the same players along different axes, and no caller wants both.

200.description: One entry per occupied proxy, plus the network total.

503.description: The session store could not be read.

get.description: Which backend servers are busy — what a server selector or `/agones` asks.

200.description: One entry per occupied server, plus the network total.

503.description: The session store could not be read. Deliberately not an empty answer: zero reads as "nobody is online anywhere", which callers will render.

get.summary: Look up names for player ids
get.description: Batched on purpose: a leaderboard page needs ten names at once, and ten round trips to render one screen is not a thing worth building. Players need not be online.

parameters.description: Repeat once per player. Ids beyond the server's cap of 100 are ignored, as are malformed ones.
parameters.name: playerId

200.description: The names that are known. Ids this service has never seen are absent from the map rather than mapped to a placeholder — including when none are known, which is an empty map and not a 404.

get.description: Tab-complete. Deliberately not "list everyone online": clients call this per keystroke, and at 10k players a full roster would be a large response sent thousands of times a second. Only players with a live session are suggested, and a blank prefix returns nothing rather than everything.

parameters.description: How many to return. Clamped to the server's maximum; absent uses it.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: What the player has typed so far. Blank or absent returns nothing.
parameters.name: prefix

200.description: Matching names, capped by the server.

get.summary: Find a session by player name
get.description: The lookup behind `/msg <name>` and `/party invite <name>` when the target is on another proxy. Matched case-insensitively: Minecraft names are unique, their casing is not.

200.description: The live session for that name.

404.description: Nobody is online under that name.

post.description: Called by a proxy as the player joins. A second login for a player who already holds a session is refused with 409 — unless the caller names a different proxy, which is what a proxy-to-proxy transfer looks like from here and takes the session over, or unless the existing session has gone quiet for longer than its TTL.

201.description: The session is now this proxy's. `Location` points at it.

400.description: `playerId` is missing or not a UUID.

409.description: The player already holds a live session elsewhere. Not an error condition — it is the answer to "may this player join", and the proxy disconnects them with an already-online message.

503.description: The session store could not be written.

post.summary: Keep a batch of sessions alive
post.description: One call per proxy per interval, naming every player it still holds. A session that stops being named expires on its own — which is how a proxy that dies without logging anyone out stops holding the network's players hostage.

400.description: The batch was empty, or an id was not a UUID. All-or-nothing on parsing: a partial success would hide the caller's bug.

503.description: The session store could not be written; nothing was touched.

put.summary: Store or clear a player's language preference
put.description: Written by the in-game `/lang` command. A null or blank `locale` clears the preference. The value is stored verbatim — the caller validates it against the languages it actually ships.

204.description: The preference was stored or cleared.

404.description: This service has never seen the player. The preference lives on the durable player row, which is written at login, so there is nothing to write against.

get.description: Read on join to seed the proxy's cache. A player who has never chosen one reads as null, and the caller falls back to the locale the client announces — that is a normal answer, not a missing resource.

200.description: The stored tag, or null when the player has never chosen one.

get.description: Who and where a player is. A proxy asks this for someone who is not connected to it — it has no other way to know they exist.

delete.description: Called by a proxy as the player leaves. Pass `proxyId`: the delete is then conditional on that proxy still owning the session, so a logout that races a transfer cannot delete the session the next proxy just created.

parameters.description: The proxy releasing the session. Omitting it deletes unconditionally, which is what an older plugin does.
parameters.name: proxyId

404.description: No session to release — already logged out, expired, or now owned by a different proxy. Nothing for the caller to do about any of them.

503.description: The session store could not be written.

put.summary: Record the backend server a player moved to
put.description: Follows a player across backend servers, so a session says where they actually are — a party warp needs the target's server, and only the proxy holding them knows when it changes.

204.description: The session now points at that server.

400.description: `playerId` is not a UUID, or `serverName` is missing.
